Here’s the consolidated 12-week couch-to-5K plan for your 24-year-old client with exercise-induced asthma, integrating base build, strength, intervals, tempo, Week-8 parkrun test, and Week-12 finisher/race-week prep. Three runs per week, two strength sessions per week. All faster work only after thorough warm-up and preferably in warm/humid or indoor settings. Always carry SABA inhaler and follow his GP’s action plan.

Global structure and safeguards
- Non-negotiables each session: 12–15 min warm-up (5 min brisk walk + dynamic mobility + 3–5 min easy jog + 2–4 short run-walk primers or 2 relaxed strides); 8–10 min cool-down walk + gentle stretches.
- Intensity anchors: Easy RPE 3–4; Steady 5; Tempo 6–7; 5K pace 7–8; Strides are relaxed fast, not sprints.
- Cold/dry air: Wear a buff/face covering, extend warm-up, cap intensity (downgrade to steady/easy), or move indoors.
- Progression rule: If symptoms escalate or recovery worsens, repeat or back off a week.

Strength (2x/week, 20–35 min; keep 24–36 h from quality runs)
- Weeks 1–4 (Foundation): Goblet/box squat 3 x 8–10; Split squat 3 x 6–8/side; RDL/hinge 3 x 8–10; Step-ups 3 x 8/side; Glute bridge 3 x 10–12; Calf raises straight and bent knee 3 x 12–15; Band row 3 x 10–12; Core: dead bug 3 x 8/side, side plank 2–3 x 20–30 sec/side; Pallof press 2 x 8–10/side optional.
- Weeks 5–8 (Strength-endurance): Progress loads/reps slightly; add lateral band walks 2 x 10–12/side; Copenhagen or advanced side planks 2–3 x 15–25 sec; hip thrusts (loaded if ready).
- Weeks 9–12 (Run-specific): Split squat FFE 3 x 6–8/side; RDL 3 x 6–8; Goblet 3 x 6–8; Single-leg hip thrust 3 x 8/side; Row 3 x 8–10; Calf complex (straight + bent + isometric hold). Optional light plyos 1x/week Weeks 9–12: 2–3 x 6–8 pogos + 2 x 6 low box step-offs (skip if any respiratory reactivity). Week 12: single light full-body session early week, 2 sets each.

Week-by-week running plan
- Week 1
  - Tue/Thu/Sat: Run 1 min, Walk 90 sec x 8–10 (RPE 3–4). Total intervals 16–24 min.

Below is a 12-week, couch-to-5K program designed for a 24-year-old with exercise-induced asthma (EIA) controlled on a SABA inhaler. It emphasizes thorough warm-ups, gradual progression, careful monitoring of symptoms, and strategies for cold-weather running. The goal is for him to run 5 km continuously by Week 12.

Key guidelines for the whole plan
- Medical and inhaler
  - Carry SABA inhaler on all runs. Consider 2 puffs 10–15 minutes before sessions if previously advised by his GP or asthma care plan.
  - Use a symptom diary (RPE, breathlessness, chest tightness, wheeze, peak flow if available). If symptoms escalate or recovery worsens, hold progression or regress one week.
- Warm-up (non-negotiable; 12–15 minutes)
  - 5 minutes brisk walk.
  - 5 minutes dynamic mobility (ankle circles, leg swings, hip openers, arm swings, thoracic rotations).
  - 3–5 minutes of run–walk “primers” (e.g., 20–30 seconds easy jog + 40–60 seconds brisk walk x 3–4).
  - Optional: warm-up mask/buff over mouth and nose in cold/dry air to humidify and warm inhaled air.
- Cool-down (8–10 minutes)
  - 5 minutes easy walk until breathing returns close to baseline.
  - Gentle lower-body stretches (calves, hamstrings, quads, hip flexors, glutes) 20–30 seconds each, 1–2 rounds.
- Intensity guidance
  - Keep most work in easy–moderate (RPE 3–5/10). He should be able to speak in short phrases.
  - Avoid surges in cold air; use progressive pacing and controlled breathing (nasal-in or pursed-lip out if helpful).
- Frequency
  - Three run-walk sessions per week (e.g., Tue/Thu/Sat). At least 48 hours between harder efforts early on.
  - Optional 1–2 low-impact cross-training days (cycling, brisk walking, elliptical, swimming in warm/humid pool) at easy effort, 20–30 minutes.
- Strength and mobility (2x/week, 20–30 minutes)
  - Focus: calves, quads, hamstrings, glutes, hips, trunk. Example circuit: bodyweight squats, split squats, hip hinge (RDL), step-ups, calf raises, side planks, dead bugs, band rows. Start 2x10–12 each, progress load slowly.
- Environment and asthma strategies
  - Prefer warmer, more humid conditions; avoid very cold, dry, windy air when possible. Use a buff/scarf as a heat–moisture exchanger in cold air.
  - Avoid high-pollen or high-pollution days if triggers apply.
  - If coughing/wheezing or chest tightness begins, slow to a walk. If not resolving with walking and controlled breathing, end the session and follow his asthma action plan.

Progression overview
- Weeks 1–4: Build consistency with run-walk intervals, increase total time from ~20 to ~30+ minutes.
- Weeks 5–8: Consolidate longer run intervals, reduce walk breaks, move toward continuous 20–25 minutes.
- Weeks 9–12: Extend continuous running to 30+ minutes, culminating in a 5K.

Week-by-week plan
Each session lists: total time and interval structure (after warm-up; always include the warm-up and cool-down described above).

Week 1 (3 sessions)
- Goal: Introduce gentle run-walk, no symptom spikes.
- Sessions (all three the same):
  - 1: Run 1 min, Walk 90 sec x 8–10 cycles (16–24 min of intervals).
  - Keep RPE 3–4. If any chest tightness, extend walk to 2–3 minutes.

Week 2 (3 sessions)
- Goal: Slightly longer total work, same easy intensity.
- Session A: Run 1 min, Walk 1 min x 10–12 (20–24 min).
- Session B: Run 90 sec, Walk 90 sec x 8–10 (20–25 min).
- Session C: Repeat Session B or Session A based on symptoms. If feeling great, choose B.

Week 3 (3 sessions)
- Goal: Extend run bouts while controlling breathing.
- Session A: Run 2 min, Walk 2 min x 6–7 (24–28 min).
- Session B: Run 2 min, Walk 90 sec x 6–8 (18–28 min; cap total at ~28).
- Session C: Run 2 min, Walk 1 min x 6 (18 min). Add an extra walk minute between sets if needed.

Week 4 (3 sessions)
- Goal: Consolidate; test slightly longer continuous segments.
- Session A: Run 3 min, Walk 2 min x 5–6 (25–30 min).
- Session B: Run 3 min, Walk 90 sec x 5–6 (22–27 min).
- Session C: Run 4 min, Walk 2 min x 4–5 (24–30 min).

Week 5 (3 sessions)
- Goal: Reduce walk time; maintain comfort.
- Session A: Run 5 min, Walk 2 min x 3–4 (21–28 min).
- Session B: Run 5 min, Walk 90 sec x 3–4 (19–26 min).
- Session C: Run 6 min, Walk 2 min x 3–4 (24–32 min).

Week 6 (3 sessions)
- Goal: Approach 20 minutes of mostly running.
- Session A: Run 8 min, Walk 2 min x 2–3 (20–30 min).
- Session B: Run 10 min, Walk 2 min x 2 (24 min).
- Session C: Run 12 min, Walk 2–3 min, Run 8–10 min (20–25 min).

Week 7 (3 sessions)
- Goal: First continuous 20 minutes if symptoms allow.
- Session A: Run 15 min, Walk 2–3 min, Run 5–10 min (20–25 min running).
- Session B: Continuous 18–20 min easy run. If symptoms, split 10 + 8 with 2 min walk.
- Session C: Run 12 min, Walk 1–2 min, Run 10–12 min.

Week 8 (3 sessions)
- Goal: Stabilize continuous 20–22 minutes.
- Session A: Continuous 20–22 min.
- Session B: Run 12 min, Walk 1–2 min, Run 12 min (or 14 + 8).
- Session C: Continuous 22–24 min if symptom-free; otherwise repeat Session A.

Week 9 (3 sessions)
- Goal: Extend to 25 minutes continuous.
- Session A: Continuous 22–24 min.
- Session B: Continuous 25 min.
- Session C: 15–18 min continuous easy + 4–6 x 30 sec very light pick-ups with 60–90 sec walk/jog between to practice relaxed cadence in warm conditions only. Skip pick-ups if cold/dry or if any symptoms.

Week 10 (3 sessions)
- Goal: Reach 28 minutes continuous.
- Session A: Continuous 24–26 min.
- Session B: Continuous 26–28 min.
- Session C: 20 min easy + 3–4 min walk + 6–8 min easy (focus on nasal-in/pursed-lip out breathing in cold).

Week 11 (3 sessions)
- Goal: 30 minutes continuous (most will be near 5K).
- Session A: Continuous 28–30 min.
- Session B: Continuous 30 min easy; practice even pacing. If cold, wear buff and extend warm-up primers.
- Session C: 20–25 min relaxed recovery jog or run-walk as needed.

Week 12 (3 sessions; event week)
- Goal: Comfortable, confident 5K.
- Session A: 20 min easy continuous.
- Session B: 10 min easy + 4 x 30 sec relaxed pick-ups (90 sec walk/jog) + 5–10 min easy.
- Session C: 5K continuous at comfortable pace. Warm up thoroughly; start conservatively, negative split if feeling good.

Strength and mobility (2x/week throughout)
- Session template (20–30 min, after a brief dynamic warm-up):
  - Lower body: Bodyweight squats 2–3 x 10–12; Split squats 2–3 x 8–10/leg; Hip hinge (RDL with light DBs) 2–3 x 8–10; Step-ups 2 x 8–10/leg; Calf raises 2–3 x 12–15.
  - Core/hips/back: Side planks 2 x 20–30 sec/side; Dead bugs 2–3 x 8–10/side; Glute bridge 2–3 x 10–12; Band row or face-pull 2–3 x 10–12.
  - Progress by small load increases or an extra set every 1–2 weeks. Keep RPE ~6–7/10, leave 2–3 reps in reserve.

Breathing and pacing tips for EIA
- Use progressive starts: first 5–8 minutes very easy jog before settling into target pace.
- Nasal breathing as tolerated early in runs; shift to nasal-in, mouth-out or pursed-lip exhalation during efforts.
- If a cough or tightness starts: slow to brisk walk, focus on long exhales, use inhaler per plan, do not re-accelerate sharply afterward.

Cold-weather adjustments
- Add an extra 5 minutes to the warm-up walk and keep the buff on until well into the session.
- Favor run-walk structure on very cold/dry days; reduce intensity rather than duration.
- Indoor alternatives (treadmill or indoor track) are encouraged on high-risk days.

Nutrition and hydration (general)
- Pre-run: Light snack 60–90 min prior if needed (banana, yogurt, small granola bar). Hydrate with water; warm beverages can feel better in cold conditions.
- Post-run: Protein 20–30 g + carbs within 1–2 hours; include electrolytes if sweating heavily or training indoors warm.
- Daily: Balanced meals emphasizing whole grains, fruits/veg, lean proteins, and healthy fats to support recovery.

Recovery and monitoring
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly.
- RPE and symptoms log after each session (breathlessness 0–10, any wheeze/tightness, peak flow if used). If two consecutive sessions show worsening symptoms or recovery, repeat the previous week.
- Red flags: Persistent chest tightness/wheeze not relieved by rest/inhaler, nocturnal symptoms post-run, needing SABA more frequently than usual—pause progression and consult GP.

Progression/Regression rules
- Progress only if sessions are completed symptom-free or with minimal, quickly resolving symptoms.
- If any session feels too hard, repeat it next time. If two sessions in a week are hard, repeat the week.
- If a session feels very easy for two consecutive weeks, you may advance one step (e.g., add 2 minutes to the continuous run) while keeping intensity easy.

By adhering to thorough warm-ups, steady pacing, and environment management, this plan builds him safely to a comfortable 5K while minimizing EIA triggers.

Here’s how to integrate a dedicated tempo run day from Weeks 7–12 without overloading him or provoking symptoms. We’ll keep three runs per week: one tempo-focused session, one interval/quality or aerobic session, and one longer easy run. Use warm, humid or indoor conditions for any faster work; default to easy running outdoors in cold/dry air.

Tempo definitions and safeguards
- Tempo effort: RPE 6–7 (comfortably hard, controlled breathing, short phrases possible). This typically aligns with his 45–60 minute race effort or “threshold.”
- Pace anchor: About 45–90 sec per mile (30–60 sec per km) faster than easy pace; or the pace he could hold for ~30–40 minutes.
- Warm-up (non-negotiable on tempo day): 12–15 minutes total: 5 min brisk walk + dynamic mobility + 4–6 min easy jog + 2 x 20–25 sec relaxed strides with full recovery.
- Cold/dry air plan: Wear a buff/face covering, extend warm-up by 5 min easy, and reduce intensity to “steady” (RPE 5–6) or move indoors.
- Asthma action: If tightness/wheeze/cough appears, downshift to easy jog or walk, focus on long exhales; use SABA per his plan; end quality if not resolving.

Weekly layout suggestion (Tue/Thu/Sat)
- Tue: Intervals or aerobic run (as per your interval layer; swap to easy if needed)
- Thu: Tempo run (new)
- Sat: Longer easy continuous run

Tempo progression (replace or modify one midweek easy/steady session)
Week 7 – Tempo primer
- Session: 10 min easy + 2 x 6 min tempo (RPE 6) with 3 min easy jog between + 5–8 min easy.
- Total quality: 12 min tempo.

Week 8 – Extend continuous time
- Session: 10 min easy + 12–14 min continuous tempo + 5–8 min easy.
- Cold adjustment: Split to 2 x 7 min tempo, 2–3 min easy between.

Week 9 – Consolidate and add a steady tail
- Session: 10 min easy + 15 min tempo + 5 min steady (RPE 5) + 5–8 min easy.
- Alternative: 3 x 6 min tempo, 2 min easy between, if he prefers breaks.

Week 10 – Threshold durability
- Session: 12 min easy + 18 min continuous tempo + 6–8 min easy.
- If form/breathing degrade, convert last 4–6 minutes to steady.

Week 11 – Tempo plus 5K-pace touches
- Session: 12 min easy + 16 min tempo + 3 x 90 sec at ~5K pace (RPE 7.5–8) with 90 sec easy jog between + 6–8 min easy.
- Cold/dry: Replace 5K touches with 3 x 60 sec steady pickups or skip them.

Week 12 – Sharpen but freshen
- Early week Session (3–4 days before race): 10–12 min easy + 12 min tempo + 3 x 20–30 sec strides (60–75 sec easy) + 6–8 min easy.
- If any symptoms or lingering fatigue: do 15–20 min steady instead, no strides.

How this meshes with intervals and long run
- Keep at least 48 hours between intervals and tempo. Example:
  - Tue: Intervals (as previously outlined; reduce volume by 1 rep during Weeks 11–12).
  - Thu: Tempo (as above).
  - Sat: Long easy run (continuous, 24–30+ minutes per your base plan).
- Quality volume cap: Keep combined time at ≥ steady effort (tempo/intervals/5K-pace) under ~20–25% of weekly total run time.
- If a week feels heavy or symptoms increase: drop intervals to aerobic easy running but keep a shortened tempo (e.g., 10–12 min) or vice versa—never both hard.

Breathing and pacing cues on tempo day
- Start the first 3–5 minutes of tempo conservatively (“float into it”).
- Cadence steady, shoulders relaxed, nasal-in/mouth-out or pursed-lip exhale to control airways.
- Even effort over even pace—mild headwind or uphill: keep RPE constant, don’t chase the watch.

Strength coordination
- Keep lower-body strength 24–36 hours away from tempo. If legs feel heavy, reduce squat/lunge sets that week by ~1 set each.
- Week 12: Only one light full-body strength session early in the week (2 sets each, no failure).

This adds a progressive, asthma-aware tempo stimulus that builds lactate threshold and pace control, dovetails with your intervals, and keeps his airway risk low by emphasizing warm-up quality, environment management, and flexible intensity.

A week-8 parkrun is a great, low-stakes benchmark—use it as a controlled tempo/strong-aerobic test, not an all-out race. Here’s how to slot it in safely and get actionable data without spiking asthma symptoms.

Purpose for Week 8
- Gauge current sustainable pace and breathing control.
- Practice full warm-up routine, pacing, and cold-air strategy.
- Establish a benchmark to set tempo and interval targets for Weeks 9–12.

Week 8 layout (Tue/Thu/Sat parkrun)
- Tue: Intervals as planned (5 x 2 min at ~10K effort, or keep aerobic if feeling taxed).
- Thu: Light tempo primer (reduce volume): 10 min easy + 10–12 min tempo (RPE 6) + 5–8 min easy.
- Sat: Parkrun test (5K) with strict “controlled effort” pacing.

Parkrun execution plan (Week 8)
- Pre-race warm-up (15–18 min, non-negotiable)
  - 5 min brisk walk.
  - Dynamic mobility: ankle rocks, leg swings, hip openers, arm swings, thoracic rotations (3–4 min).
  - 4–6 min easy jog.
  - 2 x 20–25 sec relaxed strides with 60–75 sec easy walk/jog.
  - In cold/dry air: wear a buff over mouth/nose; consider indoor pre-warm if possible. Follow his asthma plan regarding any pre-exercise inhaler use only as advised by GP.
- Pacing strategy
  - First 2 km = controlled steady/tempo (RPE 5.5–6). Do not chase groups.
  - Km 3–4 = tempo to high-tempo (RPE 6–6.5), keep breathing smooth; stay behind threshold.
  - Final 1 km = optional gentle pick-up to RPE 6.5–7 only if symptom-free and form steady.
  - Goal is even/negative split without any surges.
- Cold-weather adjustments
  - If it’s cold/dry or windy: cap effort at steady-tempo (RPE 5–6). Keep buff on until comfortably warm; remove only if breathing feels stable.
- If symptoms start
  - Downshift to easy jog or brisk walk; focus on long exhales (pursed-lip). Use SABA per action plan. Treat it as a supported training run; no heroics.

Post-parkrun cool-down and recovery
- 5–8 min easy walk/jog until breathing settles.
- Gentle lower-body stretches 20–30 sec each, 1–2 rounds (calves, quads, hamstrings, hip flexors, glutes).
- Nutrition: protein 20–30 g + carbs within 1–2 hours; hydrate. Warm fluids can feel better in cold.
- Adjust the rest of the week: no additional hard work for 24–48 hours. Replace any planned Sunday/Mon intensity with easy 20–25 min or rest.

How to use the result
- If he runs it steady-tempo (not maximal), take average pace for km 2–4 as his current tempo pace.
- If he finishes a bit harder, his overall average will sit ~10–20 sec/km faster than true tempo; subtract ~10–20 sec/km to set tempo.
- Set Week 9–11 targets
  - Tempo: aim for that derived tempo pace (RPE 6–7).
  - 5K-pace reps: ~20–30 sec/km faster than tempo pace (RPE 7.5–8).
  - Easy pace: ~60–90 sec/km slower than tempo.
- If breathing was reactive
  - Keep Week 9 intensity volume the same or 10–15% less.
  - Favor treadmill/indoor for the next quality session.
  - Reassess environment strategies (buff, longer warm-up, pre-exercise meds per plan).

Example Week 9 adjustments based on parkrun
- Tue: Fartlek 1–2–3–2–1 min at 5K–10K effort using RPE, not the watch, if outdoors and cool.
- Thu: Tempo 15 min at new tempo pace + optional 5 min steady.
- Sat: Easy continuous 25–28 min.

This makes Week 8 parkrun a smart checkpoint that sharpens pacing skill, informs training zones, and respects his asthma management.

Here’s a focused Finisher Week (race-week) you can overlay on Week 12 to sharpen, freshen, and dial race-day routines for a 5K—optimized for exercise-induced asthma. Assume a Saturday race; shift days as needed.

Objectives
- Arrive rested but sharp
- Rehearse warm-up, pacing, fueling, and cold-air strategy
- Keep airways calm: no maximal efforts, avoid cold/dry surges

Weekly overview (Mon–Sun; race Sat)
- Mon: Off or 15–20 min very easy + mobility
- Tue: Priming intervals (light)
- Wed: Off or 20–25 min easy + 6–8 min mobility
- Thu: Tempo primer (short) + strides
- Fri: Rest + shakeout option
- Sat: Race day (5K)
- Sun: Recovery

Detail by day
Mon
- Option A (rest): Walk 20–30 min + mobility (hips, calves, T-spine) 8–10 min.
- Option B (shakeout): 15–20 min very easy jog, RPE 3, then 4–5 minutes of gentle stretches.
- Breathing drill: 4–6 controlled breaths with slow 6–8 sec exhales.

Tue – Priming intervals (short, smooth)
- Warm-up 12–15 min: 5 min brisk walk + mobility + 4–6 min easy jog + 2 x 20–25 sec relaxed strides.
- Main: 2 x 3 min at ~5K pace (RPE 7.5–8) with 2 min easy jog between.
- Cool-down 6–8 min easy.
- Aim: Touch race cadence without fatigue. If cold/dry, do this indoors or cap at steady.

Wed
- 20–25 min easy jog or rest based on feel. Keep RPE 3–4.
- Mobility 8–10 min: calves, hips, T-spine, plus 3–4 long exhale breaths.

Thu – Tempo primer + strides
- Warm-up 12–15 min as above.
- Main: 10–12 min tempo (RPE 6–6.5), then 3 x 20–30 sec strides with 60–75 sec easy jog.
- Cool-down 6–8 min easy.
- If any tightness, convert to 15–20 min steady (RPE 5) and skip strides.

Fri – Rest day (option: brief shakeout)
- Option A: Full rest.
- Option B (if he feels stale): 10–15 min very easy jog + 3 x 10-sec relaxed strides, all indoors or warm conditions. Stop if any irritation.
- Logistics: Lay out kit, pins, shoes/socks, buff, inhaler. Confirm route, weather, and transport.

Sat – Race day routine (5K)
- Pre-race timing
  - 2–3 hours before: Normal breakfast he tolerates (e.g., toast + peanut butter + banana or yogurt + granola). Hydrate; warm fluids in cold weather.
  - 60–90 minutes before: Arrive, bathroom, bib, light sip of fluids.
  - 20–25 minutes before: Warm-up begins.
- Warm-up (15–18 min, non-negotiable)
  - 5 min brisk walk, buff over mouth/nose if cold/dry.
  - Dynamic mobility 3–4 min (ankle rocks, leg swings, hip openers, arm swings).
  - 4–6 min easy jog.
  - 3 x 20–25 sec relaxed strides with 60–75 sec easy jog.
  - Follow his asthma plan regarding any pre-exercise SABA use (only as advised by GP).
- Start strategy
  - First 1–1.5 km: Slightly conservative, RPE ~6–6.5; settle breathing and cadence.
  - Middle 2–3 km: Lock into goal 5K pace, RPE 7–8; keep shoulders relaxed, even effort on hills/wind.
  - Final 0.5–1 km: If symptom-free and form stable, lift to strong finish; if tightness appears, maintain or downshift—finish healthy.
- In cold/dry air
  - Keep buff on at least through the first 1–2 km; remove only if breathing remains calm.
  - Avoid sudden surges; use negative-split approach.
- Contingency for symptoms
  - Downshift to easy jog or brisk walk; emphasize long, controlled exhales. Use inhaler per plan; it’s okay to turn the day into a strong training run.

Post-race cool-down and recovery
- 5–10 min easy walk/jog until breathing normalizes.
- Gentle stretches: calves, hamstrings, quads, hip flexors, glutes (20–30 sec each, 1–2 rounds).
- Nutrition: 20–30 g protein + carbs within 1–2 hours; hydrate; warm beverage if cold.
- Note any symptoms, pacing, and perceived exertion for future planning.

Micro-taper guidelines for Week 12
- Total running time ~60–70% of Week 11.
- Keep intensity touches short and smooth (no more than 12–15 minutes total above steady for the whole week).
- Maintain strength 1x early week only: light full-body, 2 sets per exercise, no failure, stop any movement that provokes symptoms.

Gear and logistics checklist
- Shoes you’ve trained in; double-knot.
- Weather-appropriate kit; consider thin gloves and a buff.
- SABA inhaler easily accessible.
- Safety pin the bib before warm-up; plan start corral position to avoid jostling.
- If pollen/pollution is high, consider an indoor warm-up or delay higher-intensity aims.

This finisher week keeps him fresh, confident, and airway-safe while rehearsing everything he’ll do on race day—so he can toe the line calm, prepared, and ready to run his best 5K.

Here’s the consolidated 12-week couch-to-5K plan for your 24-year-old client with exercise-induced asthma, integrating base build, strength, intervals, tempo, Week-8 parkrun test, and Week-12 finisher/race-week prep. Three runs per week, two strength sessions per week. All faster work only after thorough warm-up and preferably in warm/humid or indoor settings. Always carry SABA inhaler and follow his GP’s action plan.

Global structure and safeguards
- Non-negotiables each session: 12–15 min warm-up (5 min brisk walk + dynamic mobility + 3–5 min easy jog + 2–4 short run-walk primers or 2 relaxed strides); 8–10 min cool-down walk + gentle stretches.
- Intensity anchors: Easy RPE 3–4; Steady 5; Tempo 6–7; 5K pace 7–8; Strides are relaxed fast, not sprints.
- Cold/dry air: Wear a buff/face covering, extend warm-up, cap intensity (downgrade to steady/easy), or move indoors.
- Progression rule: If symptoms escalate or recovery worsens, repeat or back off a week.

Strength (2x/week, 20–35 min; keep 24–36 h from quality runs)
- Weeks 1–4 (Foundation): Goblet/box squat 3 x 8–10; Split squat 3 x 6–8/side; RDL/hinge 3 x 8–10; Step-ups 3 x 8/side; Glute bridge 3 x 10–12; Calf raises straight and bent knee 3 x 12–15; Band row 3 x 10–12; Core: dead bug 3 x 8/side, side plank 2–3 x 20–30 sec/side; Pallof press 2 x 8–10/side optional.
- Weeks 5–8 (Strength-endurance): Progress loads/reps slightly; add lateral band walks 2 x 10–12/side; Copenhagen or advanced side planks 2–3 x 15–25 sec; hip thrusts (loaded if ready).
- Weeks 9–12 (Run-specific): Split squat FFE 3 x 6–8/side; RDL 3 x 6–8; Goblet 3 x 6–8; Single-leg hip thrust 3 x 8/side; Row 3 x 8–10; Calf complex (straight + bent + isometric hold). Optional light plyos 1x/week Weeks 9–12: 2–3 x 6–8 pogos + 2 x 6 low box step-offs (skip if any respiratory reactivity). Week 12: single light full-body session early week, 2 sets each.

Week-by-week running plan
- Week 1
  - Tue/Thu/Sat: Run 1 min, Walk 90 sec x 8–10 (RPE 3–4). Total intervals 16–24 min.
  - Goal: Consistency, zero symptom spikes.
- Week 2
  - A: 1 min run / 1 min walk x 10–12.
  - B: 90 sec run / 90 sec walk x 8–10.
  - C: Repeat A or B based on feel.
- Week 3
  - A: 2 min run / 2 min walk x 6–7.
  - B: 2 min run / 90 sec walk x 6–8.
  - C: 2 min run / 1 min walk x 6 (add extra walk as needed).
- Week 4
  - A: 3 min run / 2 min walk x 5–6.
  - B: 3 min run / 90 sec walk x 5–6.
  - C: 4 min run / 2 min walk x 4–5.
- Week 5
  - A: 5 min run / 2 min walk x 3–4.
  - B: 5 min run / 90 sec walk x 3–4.
  - C: 6 min run / 2 min walk x 3–4.
- Week 6 (introduce intervals)
  - Intervals (Tue): 10 min easy + 6 x 1 min at RPE 6 / 2 min easy jog + 5–8 min easy.
  - Easy run (Thu): 20–24 min continuous easy.
  - Long easy (Sat): 20–25+ min continuous easy.
- Week 7 (add tempo primer)
  - Intervals (Tue): 8 x 1 min at RPE 6–7 / 90 sec easy.
  - Tempo (Thu): 10 min easy + 2 x 6 min tempo (RPE 6) with 3 min easy jog + 5–8 min easy.
  - Long easy (Sat): 22–26 min continuous easy.
- Week 8 (parkrun test week; lightened quality)
  - Intervals (Tue): 12 min easy + 5 x 2 min at ~10K effort (RPE 6–7) / 2 min easy + cool-down.
  - Tempo (Thu): 10–12 min tempo only (short) + easy cool-down.
  - Parkrun (Sat): Use as controlled steady–tempo 5K test.
    - Pacing: Km 1–2 steady/tempo (RPE 5.5–6), Km 3–4 tempo (6–6.5), final 1 km optional gentle pick-up if symptom-free.
    - Full warm-up; buff in cold; treat as training, not max effort.
- Week 9 (use parkrun data to set paces)
  - Fartlek/Pyramid (Tue): 1–2–3–2–1 min at 5K–10K effort with equal-time easy jog.
  - Tempo (Thu): 10 min easy + 15 min tempo + 5 min steady + cool-down.
  - Easy (Sat): 25–28 min continuous easy.
- Week 10
  - Intervals (Tue): 4 x 3 min at high-steady/low-tempo (RPE 6.5–7) / 2 min easy jog.
  - Tempo (Thu): 12 min easy + 18 min continuous tempo + cool-down.
  - Aerobic + strides (Sat): 24–26 min easy + 4 x 20–30 sec strides.
- Week 11 (specificity builds)
  - Intervals (Tue): 5 x 3 min at goal 5K pace (RPE 7.5–8) / 2 min easy.
  - Tempo steady (Thu): 12 min easy + 16–18 min steady-to-tempo (RPE 5–6.5). Keep it smooth.
  - Easy (Sat): 20–25 min relaxed, no hard work.
- Week 12 (finisher/race week; assume Sat race)
  - Mon: Off or 15–20 min very easy + mobility.
  - Tue (Priming): 10–12 min easy + 2 x 3 min at ~5K pace (2 min easy) + 6–8 min easy.
  - Wed: 20–25 min easy or rest.
  - Thu (Tempo primer + strides): 10–12 min tempo + 3 x 20–30 sec strides.
  - Fri: Rest; optional 10–15 min shakeout if stale.
  - Sat (5K race): Full warm-up, conservative first 1–1.5 km, even effort, finish strong if symptom-free. Buff in cold. Follow asthma action plan if symptoms occur.
  - Sun: 15–25 min easy walk/jog + mobility, note symptoms and pacing.

Pacing setup from Week 8 parkrun
- Derive current tempo pace from km 2–4 average (steady–tempo effort). 5K-pace reps target ~20–30 sec/km faster than that; easy pace ~60–90 sec/km slower.

Recovery, monitoring, and nutrition
- Sleep 7–9 hours; hydrate daily.
- Pre-run snack (60–90 min prior) if desired: banana, yogurt, toast with PB; warm fluids in cold.
- Post-run within 1–2 hours: 20–30 g protein + carbs.
- Symptom log after each session (RPE, breathlessness, wheeze/tightness). If two sessions in a row worsen, reduce intensity or repeat week.
- Red flags: persistent chest tightness/wheeze not relieved by rest/inhaler, nocturnal symptoms post-run, or increased SABA reliance—pause progression and consult GP.

How to adjust for cold/dry or reactive weeks
- Move quality to treadmill/indoor track when possible.
- Otherwise keep all runs easy–steady, extend warm-up by 5–10 min, shorten or skip reps, and use a buff throughout early kilometers.

This summary ties together the full progression from couch-to-5K with strength, intervals, tempo development, a Week-8 benchmark, and a Week-12 finisher week—aimed at a confident, symptom-safe 5K.
